frozen_decisions_applied: Plan #9, verbatim: 'Derive production mDNS host exactly as zigbee-gateway-<last6>.local and advertise only https://.' -- implemented exactly for the production branch: build_gateway_mdns_host() returns "<kGatewayHostNamePrefix>-<last6-hex>" (kGatewayHostNamePrefix = "zigbee-gateway"), reusing the identical suffix convention plan #4's AP SSID already established, and main/app_main.cpp's logged URL now says https:// only when CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE is actually set (i.e. only when the listener Section 2.7 built is actually serving HTTPS).

Development builds (CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE unset) keep the plain, unsuffixed 'zigbee-gateway' hostname rather than always suffixing -- a deliberate, documented interpretation of the plan's own 'production mDNS host' wording (not 'mDNS host' unconditionally), matching the same dev/prod split #7 already established for the listener itself; per-device hostname collision is a bench-testing convenience concern in development, not a trust concern the way it is in production.

The branching decision (production-suffixed vs. plain) lives inside build_gateway_mdns_host() itself (service-layer function, internal CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE branch), not at the main/app_main.cpp call site -- matches provisioning_secret_provider.cpp's own established precedent (a single function name, internal dev/prod branching) since hostname naming is a naming decision, not a listener-composition decision the way #7's httpd_ssl_start()-vs-httpd_start() choice is.

The shared '<prefix>-<last6-hex>' logic was extracted into a private build_prefixed_gateway_suffix_name() helper rather than duplicated -- build_provisioning_ap_ssid()'s own public behavior and signature are completely unchanged, only its internal implementation now delegates to the shared helper.

build_gateway_mdns_host_implemented.detail: New function in provisioning_secrets.hpp/.cpp. Production branch (CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE=y): delegates to the same build_prefixed_gateway_suffix_name() helper build_provisioning_ap_ssid() already used, with prefix=kGatewayHostNamePrefix ("zigbee-gateway") -- requires a valid GatewayId, exactly matching plan #9's literal hostname format. Development branch: returns the plain kGatewayHostNamePrefix unsuffixed, ignoring gateway_id entirely (never fails due to an invalid GatewayId in this branch, unlike the production branch).

app_main_updated.detail: The local kGatewayHostName duplicate string constant is gone, replaced by the shared service::kGatewayHostNamePrefix (used both at the AP SSID call site and as build_gateway_mdns_host()'s internal production prefix -- single source of truth, cannot drift independently). mDNS host generation now fails closed (halts, matching every other critical-service-start failure in this file) if build_gateway_mdns_host() itself fails. The logged 'mDNS started: <scheme>://<host>.local' line now branches its own URL scheme on CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE, matching what web_server.cpp (Section 2.7) actually serves for that exact build -- the prior code unconditionally logged http://, which would have been actively wrong/misleading advice for a production build now serving real HTTPS.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Development builds keep the plain, unsuffixed 'zigbee-gateway' mDNS hostname rather than always applying the '<last6>' suffix plan #9 names.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Plan #9's own text says 'production mDNS host' specifically, and this project's #7 sub-slice already established the same dev/prod split for the listener itself (development serves plain HTTP, production serves HTTPS) -- treating hostname suffixing the same way keeps a single consistent dev/prod philosophy across this cluster, and a fixed hostname is simply more convenient for bench-testing one device.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Two development-profile zgw devices on the same LAN would still collide on the plain 'zigbee-gateway.local' hostname -- an accepted, low-stakes limitation for a bench/development scenario, not a production concern (production always gets the unique per-device suffix).
